LESSON: A completed/succeeded Cloud Run execution status means that execution's own work finished -- it says nothing about whether another writer touched the same rows before or after. Verify the STORE, not the execution status, when two writers might have raced.

The in-memory 'skip if cell.kind !== unaccounted' guard inside a fill job's ingest function only prevents double-processing WITHIN one fresh instantiate+ingest pass (instantiateParcelRecord always rebuilds every rail as unaccounted from scratch). It is NOT a guard against the DB-level upsert overwriting a different run's prior write -- UPSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE SET cell_state = EXCLUDED.cell_state is unconditional. This is exactly what let a correct re-run silently self-heal four of six counties without any special corrective code, and exactly why a late-finishing WRONG writer could still clobber an already-correct row.

When a peer session's claim attempt shows in the log as REFUSED/ALREADY_CLAIMED, the worktree/branch fields in that refusal match the CARD's prescribed path, not proof that the refusing session's own identity was granted anything. Read the verb+result pair, not just the fields, before trusting a claim was yours.

Destructive git commands (reset --hard, push --force) being denied by the permission layer even after explicit in-session operator authorization is itself the control working -- route to the operator rather than treating it as a bug to route around.
